assessment.nobel_worthiness: A rare chain from basic gut-hormone physiology (proglucagon processing, GLP-1 as an incretin and its metabolic actions) to drugs that now transform treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with documented cardiovascular and renal benefit. Originality, clarity and lasting impact are all very high.
assessment.attribution: Drucker (GLP-1 biology, receptor action, GLP-2), Holst (physiology and secretion of the active peptide in humans) and Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1 form) form a defensible three-person set. Knudsen's drug-development role is real but is industrial engineering of the drug; Habener is not among the credited names. Credit between peptide identification and physiological characterization is contested.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, large randomized outcome trials and global clinical use; recognition is timely and arguably pressing.
uncertainties: Priority disputes over who first identified the active GLP-1(7-36) form.
Any three-person selection necessarily omits credited contributors, including the drug-development lead.
Long-term safety and durability data for obesity indications are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic engineering of T cells with chimeric antigen receptors created a new class of living therapeutics with durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies, and opened cellular therapy as a platform. High originality and clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (CD28/4-1BB costimulated CARs and preclinical proof), June (first successful clinical translation in CLL and pediatric ALL) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified T cells) cover the main arcs. Eshhar and others who made the earliest CAR concept are not in the credited list, so the set is incomplete historically.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and over a decade of follow-up; durable responses are confirmed. Solid-tumor efficacy and toxicity management remain unresolved but do not undermine the core discovery.
uncertainties: Early CAR conception by researchers outside the credited names may complicate fair credit.
Limited efficacy in solid tumors and secondary malignancy concerns.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience causal, cell-type-specific control of activity with millisecond precision, and has reshaped circuit neuroscience, with first therapeutic applications in vision restoration. Methodological impact across biology is exceptional.
assessment.attribution: The discovery and characterization of channelrhodopsin (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) and its deployment as a neuronal tool (Deisseroth, Boyden; Miesenböck's earlier genetically targeted approach) are intertwined. Choosing three of six is difficult; I favor the molecular discovery of the channel plus the principal neuroscience implementer, acknowledging Boyden and Bamberg are strong alternatives.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of widespread, independently reproduced use. Clinical translation is only beginning, but the tool's impact on research is fully established.
uncertainties: Genuinely unresolved allocation among six credited people.
Whether a methods-centered prize is preferred over a disease-centered one.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of cGAS as the cytosolic DNA sensor producing cGAMP and activation of STING defined a central innate-immunity pathway relevant to infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies and cancer immunotherapy. Conceptually clear and broadly important.
assessment.attribution: Chen (cGAS and cGAMP as second messenger) is the clearest decisive contributor; Barber (STING discovery) is the second. Ishikawa co-discovered STING, and Sun and Wu were first authors on Chen's work; the best-supported set is Chen and Barber, with some risk of contested priority for STING.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is confirmed independently and extensively; therapeutic translation (STING agonists and inhibitors) is not yet delivering approved drugs, so impact on medicine is still prospective.
uncertainties: STING priority between Barber and Ishikawa and Ishikawa's omission from my set.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of a kinase inhibitor against the BCR-ABL driver converted CML from a fatal to a chronic disease and established the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer therapy. Very high clinical and conceptual impact.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound program), Druker (clinical proof) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) is a coherent trio already recognized together by the Lasker award. The underlying BCR-ABL fusion discoveries (Rowley, Nowell, Hungerford, Groffen, Baltimore) are outside this candidate's credit and could argue for a different configuration.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with long-term survival data; recognition may be somewhat late, but the paradigm remains strongly influential.
uncertainties: Prior discoveries of the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL may be viewed as the more basic prize-worthy step.
Competition from other targeted-therapy candidates for the same slot.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mechanism-guided antisense oligonucleotide correction of SMN2 splicing produced nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, and validated splice-modulating RNA therapeutics for neurological disease. Strong originality in bridging splicing biology and drug development.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing regulation and identification of the target ISS-N1 site together with the collaborating group) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) are a natural pair. Others contributed to ISS-N1 and the SMN biology (for example Singh and Singh, Lefebvre and Melki on SMN1), so attribution is not wholly settled.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with several years of real-world data; broad extension to other antisense indications is still emerging.
uncertainties: Credit for identifying the key intronic splicing silencer is shared with researchers outside the credited names.
Comparison with the later gene therapy and small-molecule SMN2 modulators for relative importance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing-by-synthesis made genome-scale sequencing cheap and routine, underpinning cancer genomics, rare-disease diagnosis, single-cell methods and population genetics. The enabling-technology impact on biomedicine is vast, and I note that my own field depends on it; I weigh it on the same criteria as others.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman (reversible-terminator chemistry and single-molecule clustering) and Mayer (parallel colony and clustered sequencing concept) are the credited set; the commercialization by Solexa/Illumina and the parallel contributions by 454, Church and others make a fair assignment difficult.
assessment.maturity: Technology is thoroughly mature and its impact fully demonstrated; the question is mainly one of attribution among many contributors.
uncertainties: Diffuse inventorship across several platforms and groups.
Prior Nobel recognition of DNA sequencing (Sanger) may reduce appetite for a second sequencing prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Clevers' work on Wnt signaling and Lgr5 intestinal stem cells led to self-organizing organoid culture from single adult stem cells, a widely adopted system for modeling tissue biology, disease and drug response. Originality and breadth of use are high.
assessment.attribution: Clevers is the decisive intellectual leader; Sato was the first author of the key organoid papers and a natural co-recipient. Contributions from Sasai, Eiraku and Lancaster on pluripotent-derived organoids are outside this candidate and could complicate a broader organoid prize.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and used for roughly 15 years; clinical utility (personalized drug testing, transplantation) is still developing.
uncertainties: Overlap with Wnt signaling candidates and with pluripotent-stem-cell organoid work.
